### Observed differences

- A02 changed from a rare, mid-trace activity into a frequent, early one: it appears in about 15 in 100 traces in the earlier window and about 65 in 100 in the later window, and its mean position moves from roughly the middle of the trace to about one-fifth in. [OCC002, POS001]
- Before, A14 passed directly to A15 in about 84 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and reached A02 in about 1 in 100; in the later window A14 leads to A02 in about 60 in 100 and to A15 in about 37 in 100, and A02 follows A14 exactly one event later in about 98 in 100 of the observed pairs, whereas the few earlier pairs were spread across gaps of one to five events. [DIR014, LAG014, REL001]
- In the later window A02 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, whereas before its successors were scattered with no share above about 21 in 100; A02 and A15 now co-occur in about 65 in 100 traces (from 15 in 100), with A02 first or interleaved with A15's repetitions. [DIR002, REL002, LAG003]
- In the middle of the process, two segments exchanged places. Before, A40 led into the always-present trio A20/A22/A23 (about 33, 25 and 25 in 100 of A40's outgoing transitions), each trio member then led to A25 in about 30–38 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A29 led to one of the alternatives A19/A21/A24 (about 31–36 in 100 each), and that alternative led to A30 in about 95–97 in 100. In the later window, A40 leads to one of A19/A21/A24 (about 40, 29 and 27 in 100), the alternative leads to A25 in about 97–98 in 100, A29 leads into the trio (about 31–33 in 100 each), and each trio member leads to A30 in about 31–33 in 100. The trio keeps its interleaved, no-fixed-order character in both windows. [DIR040, DIR020, DIR022, DIR023, DIR019, DIR021, DIR024, DIR029, REL050, REL067, OCC020, OCC022, OCC023]
- The pairwise orders reverse accordingly: A20 preceded A25 in about 99 in 100 traces before, and A25 precedes A20 in about 98 in 100 after; the same reversal holds between A29 and each of A20, A22, A23, and between A25/A29 and the alternative step. The alternative step now precedes the trio where it previously followed it (A19 before A20 rises from 0 to about 43 in 100 traces, essentially all of their co-occurrences). [REL053, REL054, REL069, REL070, REL074, REL075, REL079, REL038, REL040, REL041, REL049, REL058, REL068, REL073]
- Positions and gaps move the same way: A19, A21 and A24 shift from about two-thirds to about one-third of the way through the trace, A20, A22 and A23 from about 40% to about 64%, A25 and A29 shift slightly earlier, while A40 and A30 keep their places; the gap from A29 to A30 grows from about two events (95 in 100 pairs) to about four (94 in 100), and the gap from A40 to A25 shrinks from about four events (82 in 100 pairs) to about two (95 in 100). [POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012, POS013, LAG046, LAG057]
- The cycle A41 → A43 → A44 → back to A41 repeats more often in the later window: A41 averages about 1.8 occurrences per trace (from about 1.5), and the share of traces in which A43 and A44 repeat roughly doubles (from about 11 to about 22 in 100). [OCC040, OCC042, OCC043]
- Several side activities occur in fewer traces: A06 in about 5 in 100 (from about 22 in 100), A10 in about 6 (from 17), A04 in about 10 (from 19) and A08 in about 11 (from 16); within the alternative step, the choice shifted toward A19 (about 44 in 100 traces, from 32) at the expense of A21 (about 29, from 39) and A24 (about 28, from 32), which still almost never occur in the same trace. [OCC006, OCC010, OCC004, OCC008, OCC019, OCC021, OCC024, REL039]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A02 has become a standard step executed between A14 and A15. In the earlier window, A14 passed directly to A15 in about 84 in 100 of its outgoing transitions while A02 was a rare mid-trace activity (about 15 in 100 traces) with scattered successors; in the later window, A14 leads to A02 in about 60 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A02 follows A14 one event later in about 98 in 100 of the observed pairs, and A02 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, so most flow now runs A14 → A02 → A15 while the direct A14 → A15 edge still carries about 37 in 100. Occurrence, successor, co-occurrence, position and gap indicators all describe this same change on the same three activities, the per-window support is substantial (A02: 30 versus 129 traces; the A14-based relations: 200 traces per window), and the reference comparisons place these differences at or near the top of what random re-splits produce, so sampling variation does not plausibly explain this specific difference. The evidence cannot show how A02 behaved outside these windows, and the small share of later traces in which A02 occurs outside the A14 → A02 → A15 sequence is not characterised. [OCC002, DIR014, DIR002, LAG014, REL001, REL002, POS001]

Other differences: The middle-segment exchange described above is equally well supported, with complete order reversals between the trio A20/A22/A23 and the sequence formed by one of the alternatives A19/A21/A24 together with A25, anchored by the unchanged positions of A40 and A30. Beyond it, the cycle A41 → A43 → A44 → A41 repeats more often, A04, A06, A08 and A10 appear in fewer traces, and the choice among A19/A21/A24 shifted toward A19. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows sample two coexisting process variants in different proportions, which would produce the same window-level differences without any single process having been modified. [DIR040, DIR019, DIR021, DIR024, DIR020, DIR022, DIR023, DIR029, REL053, REL054, LAG046, LAG057, OCC040, OCC042, OCC043, OCC004, OCC006, OCC008, OCC010, OCC019, OCC021, OCC024, REL039]
